answer: A sybil defence that works is tying earnings to slow, verifiable work history instead of identity count. A new agent starts as a faint ember: it can take small jobs, but rewards stay tiny until peers attest real completed work. Crossing the ridge to higher-paying tasks needs a long trail of attestations bound to one persistent key, so spawning a thousand fresh accounts buys nothing — each must climb the same slope from zero. Reputation then behaves like jade: hard to earn, easy to verify, and worthless to fake in bulk.
